minutes_text:
INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  Library Board
  MINUTES – August 28, 2019

The Inglewood Library Board met on August 28, 2019 at the Gladys Waddingham Lecture Hall. The
meeting was called to order at 6:32 p.m. by Vice Chairman Julie Minton.

Roll Call

Present:
  Julie Minton – District 1 Board Member, Vice Chairman
  Pat Douglas – District 2 Board Member
  Ernesto Castillo – District 3 Board Member
  Jacqueline Cochran – District 4 Board Member

Absent Board Member:

  Patt Sanders – At Large Board Member, Chairman
Staff:
  Sabrina Barnes, Parks, Recreation and Community Services Director
  Frances Tracht – Library Manager
  Brenda Davis – Management Assistant

Absent Staff:
  Irina Martirosian – Staff Assistant

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Board Member Castillo made a motion for the approval of the minutes for February 27, 2019;
Board Member Douglas seconded the motion. Minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Library Board Members Castillo, Douglas, Minton and Cochran
  Nays: None

Library Report

  Frances Tracht gave verbal reports on the following items:
   The Main Library is in the process of filling two full-time Associate Librarian positions in the
  Adult Services Division. We also have put through paperwork to hire part-time Librarians
  and Library Support Clerks. At the Crenshaw-Imperial Branch Library we will be recruiting
  for a full-time Bilingual Associate Librarian. We hope to have them on board in the next six
  1
   months. San Jose State University student, Petry Saenz-Rivera, will be interning on
  Tuesdays and Saturdays for ten hours a week at Crenshaw-Imperial Branch Library.
    The Career Online High School has eight students enrolled. Two are near completion and
  four have completed the Career Online High School coursework. The Library will plan a
  graduation for the students and their families. We will work with City Administration
  through Sabrina Barnes to set a time and date so the Mayor and Council can present the
  diplomas.
    Children’s Associate Librarian, Pamela Greene, received the Digital Literacy Grant from
  California Public Utilities Commission. The Library was awarded $20,000 to implement a
  portable computer lab for children and young adults. The eight-hour curriculum includes
  an introduction to computers, art programs, “Tux Paint” and “Kid Pix 5,” a Keyboarding
  program – “Type to Learn 4,” “Comic Life 3,” as well as Microsoft Word. Students will learn
  how to search the Internet and the Library’s catalog and databases.
    Children’s Associate Librarian, Pamela Greene, received the “Maximizing Learning
  Spaces: How to MacGyver Your Library” Grant ($10,000) which enabled the Children’s
  Division to purchase new furniture, shelving and carpeting for its Early Literacy Area.
    Principal Librarian, Kerri Arroyo, received $3,000 for the “Value of Public Libraries Grant.”
  Crenshaw-Imperial Branch Library purchased laptops, a smart TV, and a projector which
  enabled us to create a classroom environment for special need students.
    Principal Librarian, Kerri Arroyo, received “Lunch at the Library Grant.” Main and
  Crenshaw-Imperial Branch Library will split $13,000. This grant is to enhance the Summer
  Reading Programming and lunch at each site.
    Summer Reading Program was successful due to the grant we received. Unfortunately,
  the number of readers and books read were low but the number of attendees at programs
  were high.
    Inglewood Public Library has a partnership with West Los Angeles College for non-credit
  College courses available for Junior High and up. Currently at Crenshaw-Imperial Branch,
  courses are provided for the Uniquely-Abled Adults. When completed students will receive
  certificates. Fall classes will start at Crenshaw-Imperial Branch on Thursday, September
  5, 2019 on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. The goal at the Main
  Library is to provide this program to High School students to begin in the fall.
    Staff elevator has been renovated and is working.
    Constitution and Citizenship Week is Tuesday, September 17, 2019 thru Saturday,
  September 21, 2019. There will be games, films, treats and prizes at Main and Crenshaw-
  Imperial Branch Library.

Friends Report

  Frances Tracht told Board Members there will be a Friends of Inglewood Public Library winter book
sale on Saturday, September 14, 2019 from 10:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m.

Public Comments

  None

Commissioner Comments

  2
   Board Member Minton, Douglas, Castillo and Cochran have numerous concerns of the Library
regarding the roof, carpet, furniture and painting of the Library. Sabrina Barnes told Board Members the
City is aware of their concerns and have been discussing what approach to remedy the above concerns
and/or take a global approach to renovate the Library.

  Board Member Cochran is happy with the progress at both Libraries.

  Board Member Castillo wanted to know the procedure for taking pictures on programs in the
Library and putting it on social media. Sabrina Barnes told him you must have written approval to take
photos or (photo replacements). There have to be signs posted stating if you are in this area filming and
photos may take place.

  Board Member Douglas stated she attend the Library’s staff meeting last week and watched the
film called “The Public” with staff.

  Board Member Castillo thanked Gregory Mason for coming out to the Library Board meeting.

  Board Member Minton wanted to know what is going on with Morningside Park Branch Library.
Sabrina Barnes told her the City is looking for funds for that Branch.

With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 7:16pm.
